options.lead: Every ride here is a physics model, running in blocks.
lines: Click a ride. Press Program. Change a number.
Predict first, then press Save and measure.
options.footnote: In this lab, 1 foot of the world is 1 metre. There is no air resistance.

options.subtitle: Everything falls at the same rate

options.title: Time goes by one dt at a time
options.caption: Click the car, press Program, change a green number.

options.title: Time to fall a height h
options.body: t = square root of (2h / g). From 20 m that is 2.02 s, at 19.8 m/s. Mass is not in it. Try g = 1.62 for the Moon and 3.71 for Mars.

options.title: Drop the blue ball from 10 m
options.target: Click the blue ball (no green arrow), press Program:
options.tip: 0.2 is g × dt: 9.8 × 0.02, near enough. Pick each name from the little arrow.

options.title: Split the speed in two

steps.text: set cosA to cos° of angle
set sinA to sin° of angle

options.caption: Click the ball. Change speed or angle. Save fires it.

options.title: How far a shot goes
options.body: Range = v squared x sin(2 x angle) / g. At 20 m/s and 45 degrees: 40.8 m, up to 10.2 m high. Press the green arrow again to draw another arc beside it.

options.title: Land in the ring at 30 m
options.target: Click the yellow-and-black ball, press Program:

steps.text: press Save and watch where it lands

options.tip: Work the speed out from the formula before you press Save. It takes one try if you do.

options.title: a = F / m
options.caption: Click a cart. Change force, mass or mu.

options.title: Four times the mass
options.body: 400 N on 100 kg gives 4 m/s squared. On 400 kg it gives 1 m/s squared. Time them over 40 m. Then set mu to 0.05 and see what friction takes.

options.subtitle: Energy changes form. It does not go away.

options.title: Speed from energy

steps.text: set v to square root of v2

options.caption: Click the round pod. Change height (up to 18), mu or mass.

options.title: What the drop is worth
options.body: m g h = one half m v squared, so v = square root of (2 g h). A 15 m drop gives 17.1 m/s, and mass cancels. The track's slope is 30 degrees and 30 m long to that height.

options.title: CLICK ME TO CHANGE THE CRASH
lines: u1, u2: their speeds, toward each other (m/s)
Both cars read what this board works out.

options.title: Add up the momentum
options.caption: Click the scoreboard. Change a mass, a speed or e.

options.title: No outside force, no change
options.body: A's 150 x 4 less B's 300 x 1 is 300 kg m/s before, and the same after. Set e to 0: momentum still holds, but motion energy falls from 1350 J to 100 J.

options.title: Add a third car, watching
options.target: Click the green car, press Program:
options.tip: It uses the numbers the scoreboard shares. Change u1 there, and this car changes too.

options.subtitle: Period, and the force toward the middle

options.title: Swing back toward the middle

steps.text: set s to sin° of angle

options.caption: Click the boat. Change length (up to 14) or angle.

options.title: What sets the period
options.body: T = 2 pi x square root of (L / g), for small swings. L = 12 m gives 6.95 s. The weight of the boat is not in it. Compare 30 degrees with 5 degrees and see how good "small" has to be.

options.title: Why the chains lean
options.body: cos(lean) = g / (w squared x L). Going round in 6 s on 14 m chains, the lean is 50.3 degrees and the chair runs 10.8 m out. Click the cap on top and change the period.
